name: doory
text: Paying for Canva Pro just to make posts and thumbnails? There's a free, open source one called Doory. It's a design editor that runs in your browser. Posters, stories, slides, thumbnails, even resumes. Edit the text, drag in shapes and icons, and remove a background right in the browser. Add animations, page transitions and music, then export as MP4 or GIF. No paid plan, no locked features, no ads. You host it yourself with Docker, and it's still early, with ten templates so far. Comment DOORY and I'll send you the link.

name: ecc5
text: Most people use Claude Code with zero plugins. ECC is a free one with over ninety commands. Here are five worth stealing. One: plan. It writes the plan and waits for your OK before touching code. Two: build-fix finds your build errors and fixes them with small, safe changes. Three: orch-fix-defect proves the bug with a failing test first, then fixes it until it's green. Four: test-coverage finds the gaps and writes the missing tests. Five: santa-loop. Two separate reviewers both have to approve before your code ships. Comment ECC and I'll send you the link.

name: taste
text: Your coding agent can build a website. But does it ever look at it? Taste Skill makes it look. It's a free, open source skill for Claude Code and Codex. First, it picks one of twenty art directions. Then it builds with real photos from open archives, and credits them. Then it opens the page in a real browser at three widths, studies its own screenshots, and fixes the top three problems. Up to three rounds. A page takes thirty to forty-five minutes and a lot of tokens. Comment TASTE and I'll send you the link.
